newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London lower after Wall Street slip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London lower after Wall Street slip.

text.p: U.S. shares were generally lower on Friday following Wall Street's sluggish performance on Thursday but trade was light as investors remained cautious about the Dow's near-term prospects.
"The Dow was overbought and has come down the past two days but perhaps not enough," one market maker said.
"We might see a bit more profit-taking today."
The Dow Industrials Average slipped 20.47 points to 6,792.25 on Thursday, despite a eight percent surge in IBM shares.
Weaker U.S. treasuries depressed sentiment, another dealer said, noting that the yield on the 30-year long bond continued to creep slowly toward the 7.20 percent resistance level.
The June T-bond was down 2/32 to 107-8/32 while the yield on the cash 30-year long bond was standing at 7.14 percent by 1040 GMT.
"Strong earnings brought the Dow back from the brink over the past couple of weeks. Companies are doing well because the U.S. economy is booming." the dealer said.
"But the bonds are telling us that the Fed is bound to raise rates to cool things down which will also take the heat out of earnings toward the end of the year."

Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International also expects and earnings slowdown due to the continued strength of the dollar, which is trading at three to four year highs against the mark and the yen.
"we will start to see the impact of the dollar on earnings in the third and fourth quarters," Shah said. I think the risk is still to the downside for the Dow."
IBM, which soared $11-3/8 in New York after impressive first-quarter profits, was down $1/2 to $153-1/4. Intel Corp slipped $3/8 to $145-3/4.

Elsewhere, Ford Motor Co added $1/8 to $34-5/8 after news that the automaker's Hertz rental car business, which is due to make its debut on the New York Stock Exchange on Friday, would be priced at the top end of market expectations.
Lead underwriter JP Morgan said on Thursday that Hertz would be priced at $24 but IPO specialists think the share could race much higher at the start.
"It's going to be a big, booming opening," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

After today's initial public offering, Ford will own more than 50 percent of class A shares, and all of the Class B shares in Hertz, the world's largest rental car company in terms of revenue and fleet size.
